cards.text: Paul the apostle is writing a letter to Timothy, his true child in the faith, about how to lead the church. Now Paul brings up a problem. Somebody teaches another doctrine and disagrees with the sound words of our Lord Jesus Christ and with godly teaching.

cards.question: Paul says the person teaching against the sound words of Jesus really understands the truth and just explains it badly.

cards.text: Instead of the truth, Paul says this guy has an unhealthy interest in controversies and disputes about words. FORTY messages in the group chat, friend. All of them fighting over ONE word.

cards.question: Paul says something comes out of all those disputes about words. What is it?

answers.text: Envy and strife and evil suspicions

cards.text: On top of that comes constant friction between men of depraved mind who are devoid of the truth. And Paul says these men have their own idea of what godliness is for.

cards.question: Paul is describing men of depraved mind who are devoid of the truth. What do they think godliness is for?

cards.text: Here's the twist, friend. Paul says there IS great gain in godliness, but only when it's paired with one other thing.

cards.question: Paul says godliness with ___ is great gain.

cards.text: Then Paul explains why. And he goes ALL the way back to the day you showed up in this world.

cards.question: Paul talks about coming into the world and leaving it. What does he say we bring in and carry out?

answers.text: Nothing in and a little out
A little in and nothing out

cards.text: Me? I came out of a bakery bin with a 25-cent price sticker, and that was my WHOLE estate. So Paul keeps the list of what we really need SHORT.

cards.question: Paul says if we have ___ and ___ we will be content with these.

cards.text: Then Paul looks down the other road: people who want to be rich.

cards.question: Paul says those who want to be rich fall into ___.

cards.text: And they get ensnared by many foolish and harmful desires. Ensnared, friend, like me the day my mustache got caught in the dough mixer and I went around and AROUND and AROUND.

cards.question: Paul says the foolish and harmful desires of those who want to be rich plunge them into ruin and destruction.

cards.text: Then Paul digs all the way down to the root under all of it. And he's careful about exactly what that root is.

cards.question: Paul says money itself is the root of all kinds of evil.
Paul says some people craved money. What happened to them and the faith?
Paul says those who craved money ended up pierced with many sorrows. Who pierced them?

findings.problem: The card turns Paul's conditional into a plain statement. The text says 'If anyone teaches another doctrine,' but the card says 'Somebody teaches another doctrine.'

The card uses facts from outside the passage that have no reference. Timothy as Paul's 'true child in the faith' comes from 1 Timothy 1:2, and the letter being 'about how to lead the church' comes from 1 Timothy 3:14-15. The card cites only 1 Timothy 6:3.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: 'There IS great gain in godliness, but only when it's paired with one other thing' adds an 'only' that the text doesn't have. Verse 6 says godliness with contentment is great gain. It doesn't say godliness is gain only under that condition.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The joke is about verse 7 (bringing nothing into the world), but the card cites verse 8. 'So Paul keeps the list...' ties Papa Dorin's price-sticker story to Paul's reasoning, as if one followed from the other. It also calls verse 8 'the list of what we really need,' but the text talks about being content with food and clothing, not about what we need.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: 'He's careful about exactly what that root is' tells the baker the next true-or-false statement is a trick. That points them to False on card 18 instead of letting them reason it out. It also adds a reason for how Paul writes that the text doesn't give.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
